reading.body:
InVideo sells AI video editing as a natural-language agent that operates a real multitrack timeline, not as a model or an infrastructure story.

The record is a single product entry and a short profile. It says what the company offers and who it is aimed at, editors rather than AI specialists, and it says the user can take over at any frame. That is a product-positioning fact, not a capability claim, and nothing in the data measures how well the agent performs.

There is no compute, building, or power information here. No chip counts, no data center footprint, no energy contract, no litigation, no MCP server, no SEC or patent facts. A video generation tool of this kind does consume inference compute, but this data does not quantify it, so no claim about InVideo's draw on the grid can be made from it.

What the record does establish is narrow and worth stating plainly: InVideo is an application layer company, and the data covers its product and pitch only. It does not cover cost, scale, model provenance, or any dependency on physical infrastructure.
